text:
sam_k: Heads up — opening a PR to change how gpupool handles KMS and provider scoping. goal is to avoid repeated plan diffs when our gitops runner picks different region providers for canary vs prod.

jordan_r: can you TL;DR the root cause? why are we seeing diffs?

sam_k: tl;dr: gpupool module currently inherits the root aws provider. when Argo job runs in us-west-2 it provisions a regional aws_kms_key, then another run in us-east-1 (or a different provider alias) causes TF to want to replace or recreate keys because they are tied to different provider instances. also provider upgrades (aws v4->v5) changed default endpoints which made aliasing more sensitive.

mike: ugh, I saw that — plan shows kms_key.diff "provider change" and then terraform wants to recreate resource. consequences: brief capacity loss while node pools reprovision.

anya: quick mitigation is to pin provider alias inside the module or accept kms as an input (kms_key_arn) so the module doesn't create keys in mixed regions.

sam_k: exactly. proposed patch in PR #3456: split out a small submodule resources/kms.tf and require passing providers = { aws = aws.<region_alias> } when using regional pools. snippet:```hcl
module "gpupool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwood/modules/gpupool.git?ref=v2.4.0"
  providers = { aws = aws.us-west-2 }
  name = "gpu-usw2"
  kms_key_id = var.kms_key_id
}
```

mike: for existing state we need a safe migration plan. I suggest: run in staging -> terraform state list | grep module.gpupool -> terraform state mv module.gpupool.aws_kms_key.gpukey module.gpupool.aws_kms_key.gpukey_new (or use state replace-provider) and then import or rename resource in new module layout. avoid destroy/create in prod.

anya: yes. exact commands I've used before:```bash
# on a copy of state or in staging workspace
terraform state mv module.gpupool.aws_kms_key.gpukey module.gpupool.module.kms.aws_kms_key.gpukey
terraform plan -target=module.gpupool.module.kms
```

linh: small note on IAM: if we move keys around make sure the node-role has kms:Decrypt/Encrypt for the new key id and that KMS key policy includes the account principal used by autoscaling launch templates. otherwise nodes might fail to boot when mounting encrypted AMIs.

devops: CI change I propose: when module version bump is detected, run an automated plan in the staging GitOps pipeline and tag the ArgoCD canary app with the module ref. only after manual approval do we promote the tag to production appset. this reduces cross-region overlap during rollout.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] canary apply succeeded for gpupool-staging @ 2025-07-15T14:12:30Z :white_check_mark:

mike: cost/regulatory note — creating a new KMS key per region has small monthly charge and additional API calls for rotation. prefer central shared CMK per environment unless customers require separate regional keys.

sam_k: final rollout plan (short): 1) merge v2.4.0 with provider alias support behind feature flag 2) run state-migration in staging workspace, verify plan shows no replacements 3) run canary apply via ArgoCD for one small pool 4) wait 24h, perf/health check 5) promote module ref to prod apps 6) deprecate old behavior and document provider/ kms inputs in module README.

jordan_r: sounds good. can you add the state mv commands to the PR description and mark as manual step? I don't want automation doing state moves.

sam_k: yep will add exact commands + rollback notes. adding a checklist in the PR and a short ops-runbook entry.

jordan_r: :thumbsup:

linh: I'll run the preflight IAM/KMS checks before the canary apply and post results here.

mike: and I'll schedule a quick maintenance window if any pool needs transient reprovisioning.

sam_k: thanks all — PR is up: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/pulls/3456 — ping me for walkthrough.
